**
Jagmohan Bansal, J. (Oral)
1.

The petitioner through instant petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India is seeking
direction to respondent No.2 to decide his revision petition against order dated 23.04.2025 passed
by Senior Superintendent of Police, Mohali.
2.  The petitioner joined Punjab Police Force as Constable on 26.06.1972.
He from time to time was promoted to higher Ranks.

He was implicated in FIR No.6 dated 11.01.2022 under Sections 419,
420, 464, 465, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short '1PC') (Section 201 IPC and Sections 7-A and 13 of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 added later on) registered at Police Station, Sector 3 (North), U.T. Chandigarh.
He vide order dated 23.02.2022 was suspended from service and subjected to departmental inquiry.
He was served show cause notice on 23.11.2023 proposing punishment of dismissal from service.
He vide order dated 23.04.2025 was awarded punishment of dismissal from service.
He preferred an appeal which came to be dismissed vide order dated 27.06.2025 1 of 2 by Appellant Authority.
He on 04.08.2025 preferred revision before Director General of Police, Punjab which is still pending adjudication.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that grievance of the petitioner, at this stage, would be redressed, if respondent No.2-Director General of Police, Punjab is directed to decide his revision petition in a time bound manner.
4.

Mr. Aman Dhir, Deputy Advocate General, Punjab, who on advance notice is present in Court on behalf of respondent-State, assures the Court that competent authority would consider and decide petitioner's revision petition within three months from today.
